core_obligations: Replace X-bar by its normalization: the normalization morphism is finite and X-bar^nu is a variety, and since X is normal the restriction over X is an isomorphism, so X-bar may be assumed normal (proof lines 5166-5177).

List the generic points xi_1, ..., xi_r of the complement of X in X-bar, which are finite in number because X-bar is Noetherian, and let J be the set of indices with dim(O_i) = 1; for j in J the ring O_j is a discrete valuation ring giving a valuation v_j on k(X-bar)^* (proof lines 5190-5206).

Prove that the kernel of O(X)^* to the product over j in J of Z, f maps to the product of v_j(f), equals k^*: for f in the kernel and an affine open Spec(B), every height one prime q of B corresponds to a point which is either some xi_j or lies in X, so f lies in B_q for all height one q, hence f lies in B (proof lines 5208-5235).

Conclude that such an f extends to a global section of O over the proper X-bar, and since k is algebraically closed it lies in k, so the kernel is k^* and the quotient is a subgroup of the finitely generated group Z^{#J} (proof lines 5235-5239).
proof_roadmap: Normalize X-bar to reduce to the normal case (proof lines 5166-5177).
Build the valuations attached to the one dimensional local rings at the generic points of the boundary (proof lines 5190-5206).
Compute the kernel of the resulting map by the height one localization criterion (proof lines 5208-5235).
Use properness and algebraic closedness of k to pin the kernel down to k^* (proof lines 5235-5239).
difficulty_reason: For an algebraically closed field k, a proper variety X-bar over k and an open subscheme X which is normal, the lemma shows that O^*(X)/k^* is a finitely generated abelian group (statement lines 5156-5163). The proof has three real moves: first replace X-bar by its normalization, using that the normalization morphism is finite and is an isomorphism over the normal X, so that X-bar may be assumed normal (proof lines 5166-5177); then let xi_1, ..., xi_r be the generic points of the complement of X and single out the indices j for which the local ring O_j is one dimensional, so that O_j is a discrete valuation ring and yields a valuation v_j on k(X-bar)^* (proof lines 5190-5206); finally show that the kernel of O(X)^* to the product of the Z over j in J is k^*, by proving that an element of the kernel lies in every height one localization of every affine piece, hence extends to a global function on the proper X-bar and therefore lies in k. The claim is H2: every input is standard, but the assembly of the height one localization criterion with properness into the finiteness statement is the non-formal part.
